title: Two-dimensional separable and coupled Wannier-reduction exercise
status_detail: Human accepted and closed at RM-PERIODIC-2D-FINAL-ACCEPTANCE-HC05. The scalar and corrected rank-three composite routes, retained Wannier90 preprocessing failure, converged balanced-embedding reference, six-case non-DFT Wannier90 sensitivity study, and separate Qi--Wu--Zhang, Hofstadter, and Haldane controls and phase sweeps remain calculated and independently verified. Native Berry-link and common finite-supercell spreads remain separate. The nonmonotone mesh, cutoff, and embedding cases explicitly do not support a converged or embedding-independent localization claim, and no unfavorable case was retried or discarded. A checksummed local native-evidence archive is prepared but not published or transmitted. Acceptance establishes completion only for the declared synthetic numerical-verification scope; it does not establish material adequacy, scientific validation, transferability, uncertainty quantification, or a general localization theorem, and it does not authorize DFT, publication, release, or successor activation.
objective: Extend the verified one-dimensional exercise to a separable square-lattice reference and then a controlled nonseparable coupling, exposing genuinely two-dimensional representation and reduction issues.
authorized_scope: Plan exact separable product and Kronecker-sum checks before introducing anisotropy or nonseparable coupling.

Develop full-mesh representation comparison, degeneracy-projector matching, gauge-loop closure, topology diagnostics, directional hopping shells, effective-mass tensors, and direct-versus-mediated reductions.
Increase coupling through a frozen sequence while keeping numerical, subspace, gauge, localization, and model-class controls explicit.
completion_criteria: The separable limit reproduces the retained one-dimensional energies, projectors, products, and hopping structure under a fixed ordering.
Two-dimensional cutoff, mesh, degeneracy, gauge, topology, shell, fitting, and coupling-continuation effects are separately verified or reported unresolved.
Results remain illustrative numerical verification and identify failure modes before any three-dimensional multiorbital material reduction.
exclusions: No claim about a two-dimensional material, silicon, production Wannier localization, scientific validation, or public scientific API stability is authorized.
A high-symmetry path does not replace the full reciprocal mesh for operator or localization checks.
Completion does not authorize material-specific DFT or automatic succession.
